chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Fadala from Rifah ibn Musa, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'When Ali (peace be upon him) rose from the first two rak'ahs, he would say: "By Your power and strength, I rise and I sit."'
ai.seo_question: What supplication did Imam Ali recite when rising from the first two rak'ahs of prayer?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith highlights the Prophetic tradition of reciting 'Bi-hawlika wa quwwatika' upon rising from the first two rak'ahs, a practice deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence as a recommended (mustahabb) act of humility. It underscores the theological principle that even the physical movements of worship are sustained by divine grace rather than human capability alone. This specific dhikr serves as a bridge between the recitation in the standing position and the subsequent bowing, reinforcing the continuity of remembrance throughout the prayer.
